Create PNU cohort arguments

Source: R/SettingsObjects.R
createPnuCohortArgs.Rd

Specifies which cohorts play the roles of reference treatment (A), new treatment / switcher events (B), and outcome, along with covariate filters and population-size limits.

Usage

createPnuCohortArgs(
  targetCohortId,
  comparatorCohortId,
  outcomeCohortId,
  excludedCovariateConceptIds = integer(0),
  includedCovariateConceptIds = integer(0),
  washoutPeriod = 365,
  maxCohortSize = 0
)

Arguments

targetCohortId

(`integer(1)`) Cohort ID for treatment A (reference treatment; patients must be on this treatment before the index date).

comparatorCohortId

(`integer(1)`) Cohort ID for treatment B (the new treatment; switcher index events are the start dates in this cohort).

outcomeCohortId

(`integer(1)`) Cohort ID for the outcome of interest.

excludedCovariateConceptIds

(`integer`) Concept IDs to exclude when constructing covariates (e.g. drugs directly on the causal pathway). Default: `integer(0)` (none excluded).

includedCovariateConceptIds

(`integer`) Concept IDs to include when constructing covariates. An empty vector means all concepts are included. Default: `integer(0)`.

washoutPeriod

(`integer(1)`) Minimum days of continuous observation required before a subject's cohort start date. Default: `365`.

maxCohortSize

(`integer(1)`) Maximum number of subjects in each cohort. `0` means no limit. Default: `0`.

Value

A `PnuCohortArgs` R6 object.

References

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell'Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. *Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf* 2017;26(4):459-468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

Examples

args <- createPnuCohortArgs(
  targetCohortId = 1,
  comparatorCohortId = 2,
  outcomeCohortId = 3
)
